notes: Profile: mid-stage developer tooling company building an internal developer search + code intelligence product.
Primary pain: current self-hosted Elastic + custom embeddings pipeline can't scale beyond 10M vectors without large query latency spikes and high infra costs.
Workload specifics: ~25M code embeddings today (repo snapshots + CI artifacts), reindex delta daily, full snapshot weekly; planning to hit 100M vectors in 12-18 months.

Reranking requirement: two-stage pipeline — cheap ANN recall (HNSW/FAISS) -> cross-encoder rerank for top-50 candidates. Want Redwood to support hybrid rerank flow and low-latency cross-encoder fallback.

Latency targets: p50 < 80ms, p95 < 250ms for developer query flows; background batch indexing can be higher but on-demand reindexing (hot docs) should be sub-500ms for single-doc upserts to be visible to search.
Throughput: typical peak 120 QPS dev traffic; internal CI jobs spawn 500 concurrent reindex tasks overnight; care about batching and cost tradeoffs.
Cost sensitivity: tight unit economics — target < $0.002 per query (recall+rerank amortized) at 50M vector scale; willing to trade slight latency for cost savings via quantization & caching.
Model preferences: open embedding models (4-8k context embeddings), quantized candidate models for reranker; want recommendation on model/quantization profiles from Redwood Optimize.
Security: mandatory SSO/SAML + SCIM for provisioning, audit logs for developer queries, retention controls and EU data residency for certain client repos.
Deployment: evaluating Redwood Private (VPC) with optional on-prem connectors for air-gapped clients. Dedicated pool for rerank cross-encoder models to meet p95 SLA.

POC ask: 1) ingest 25M embeddings into a test index, 2) demonstrate rerank latency with our cross-encoder on dedicated pool, 3) nightly delta reindex test showing KV/prefix caching benefits, 4) cost projection for 50M and 100M scenarios.
Quote from CTO: 'We need a serving layer that scales without doubling infra every quarter — and SAML that just works. Show us predictable unit economics.'
AE notes: very technical buying group (CTO, infra lead, security), quickest path is focused POC addressing latency + cost per query, then procurement for Dedicated/Private.
SE notes: initial proof-of-concept script available, provided sample embed pipeline and FAISS snapshots. Engineering wants streaming rerank hook and model fallbacks for degraded capacity.
Procurement note: Procurement expects enterprise contract language (data residency, termination, indemnities) — legal has their standard redlines.
Internal ops: ask from Halcyon to provide a network peering template and SCIM connector docs before next security review.
Meeting outcomes: Redwood Dedicated looks favorable; Private needed for EU-resident customer pipeline. Next demo to include cost breakdown by batching config.
